items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: I did a lot of club playing with Don Menza and the sextet

ctx.x: Yeah. Bobby said that my wife could tell by the look on my face how my day went in the studios when I got home.

Oh yeah, of course Lisa could. You know Bobby decided after — you know he could have done what I did in the studios, but he decided to teach and go out and play jazz, he wanted to do that. He didn’t want to be in the studios like I did. I mean he would have enjoyed it and loved a lot of the stuff but he really wanted to be freer than that. He wanted to be a bird, a flying bird playing jazz you know. I didn’t have the hours that he had to do it because I was in the studio. And I’d have to go out on weekends and do…

If you had an offer to do like a three week tour with some fantastic band that was put together to do a tour of the country, would that have been hard for you, like you’re taking yourself out of the scene and you’re not making the dates people want?

items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: When he was in the hospital I remember going to see him. I was on my way to Europe and Chuck Findley and I and Joe Romano to see him.

ctx.x: I really enjoyed your perspective on him because—

It’s different from what you — I mean it’s unreal. When he was in the hospital I remember going to see him. I was on my way to Europe and Chuck Findley and I and Joe Romano to see him. We had a ride to the airport so we stopped at UCLA and this was just after his operation, and his left arm was gone, his left arm was totally paralyzed. We never saw him again. He had died while we were in Europe and his left arm was paralyzed. And he’d be laying there. And every time he’d yawn, his arm would raise. There was…
